{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Gibraltar|Cuisine of Gibraltar]]

'''Rosto''' is a dish is of [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italian]] origin, and provides for two complete courses cooked in one pot without the need for an oven. Originally the pasta was served as a first course with the tomato sauce over it. This was followed by the sliced meat, usually a cheaper cut of pork instead of loin and a small piece at that, with the potatoes, carrots and mushrooms.

It is still extremely popular although many people nowadays also cook it with chicken thighs or even a piece of beef instead of the traditional pork.

== Ingredients ==
 
* 1 [[Cookbook:Kg|kg]] [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] loin
* 2 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], cut in quarters
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* ½ kg penne or macaroni [[Cookbook:Pasta|pasta]]
* ¼ kg [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]]
* ½ kg fresh [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* 1 tin ‘[[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomate triturado]]’ (tomato paste, or three peeled, de-seeded and puréed tomatoes)
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic clove]]
* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]] (for [[Cookbook:Frying|frying]])
* [[Cookbook:Wine|White wine]]
* [[Cookbook:Sugar|Sugar]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Grater|Grated]] [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]] (Edam or [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmesan]])

== Procedure ==

# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] crushed garlic clove and chopped onions until soft. 
# Add tomatoes; fry for 5 minutes, then add pork loin and brown until sealed.
# Add tin of ''tomate triturado'' and a dash of white wine. 
# Add potatoes and carrots, then cook until meat, potatoes and carrots are done.
# Add the mushrooms about 10 minutes before the end.
# Add salt, pepper and sugar to taste. 
# [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] the macaroni until [[Cookbook:Al Dente|al dente]]. 
# Remove the meat from the stew and [[Cookbook:Slicing|slice]].
# Serve meat, potatoes and pasta on same plate, pouring sauce over pasta and topping with grated cheese.
